verdict.rationale: Name.com documents a Create Domain endpoint that registers a domain under your account, plus availability checks and a sandbox for automated tests, so purchase-by-API fits a deploy script. Contact management is mentioned only in a summary list. No evidence shows a documented call for setting nameservers: DNS record creation is a different capability, and the bulk nameserver change described by a user is a UI feature. missing for 10: documented nameserver-setting call, detailed contact-setting parameters in the registration/contacts reference, independent hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end scripted registration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can register a domain end to end via the API — purchase, contacts, and nameservers in documented calls, so registration can be part of a deploy script

citations.quote: Registers a new domain under your account. You must provide `domain.domainName` at minimum. This endpoint is commonly used to programmatically onboard new domains through user signup flows or checkout experiences.
Checks whether up to 50 domain names are purchasable and returns **discovery** pricing for each result.
manage domain settings (locks, privacy, autorenew, contacts)

provides a **sandbox (testing) environment** that mirrors production request/response shapes, so you can build and run automated integration tests without affecting real domains or incurring real charges
